routes.description: Establish that Paul's language and historically proximate testimony are best explained by his understanding Jesus as an earthly Jewish person whose family, associates, teachings, and execution belonged to human history.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the cumulative Pauline references are more coherently read as earthly biography, the crucifying rulers and familial language receive credible human and biological readings, and Luke-Acts can materially connect Paul's circle to a historical Jesus tradition.

motionBridge.description: Show that Paul's surviving claims are better explained by an earthly historical Jesus than by a death and resurrection confined to a mythic heavenly realm.

centralBridges.description: Establish that Paul's references to ancestry, birth, teachings, associates, betrayal, death, and resurrection cumulatively locate Jesus within earthly Jewish history.
Establish from the context and usage of First Corinthians that the rulers involved in Jesus's crucifixion were human authorities, even if demonic participation is also allowed.
Establish that Paul's references to the Lord's brothers plausibly concern biological kin and that historically informed testimony from Paul's traveling circle coheres with an earthly Jesus.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Justify the scope of Pauline material admitted to the inquiry where disputed authorship affects the available biographical evidence.
Support the historical proximity and reliability of Luke-Acts and related narratives through first-person travel material, external corroboration, and interlocking incidental details.

routes.description: Establish that the authentic Pauline evidence does not unambiguously place Jesus's salvific career on earth and is coherently explained as a heavenly cosmic event later supplied with earthly narrative settings.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if Paul's key language remains compatible with celestial agents, settings, and non-biological brotherhood, while Luke-Acts and Gospel narratives cannot independently supply reliable evidence of what Paul understood about Jesus.

motionBridge.description: Show that Paul's authentic letters are at least better explained by a mortal-bodied Jesus dying and rising in a mythic heavenly realm than by an earthly historical career.

centralBridges.description: Establish that the authentic Pauline letters never unambiguously locate Jesus's life, death, burial, or resurrection on earth and permit a heavenly cosmic reading.
Establish that the crucifying rulers can be celestial powers and that ancient cosmology supplied heavenly counterparts of earthly places and practices sufficient for a celestial crucifixion.
Establish that Luke-Acts and the Gospels lack the authorship, independence, or historical reliability required to infer Paul's own conception of Jesus from their earthly narratives.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that Paul's references to brothers of the Lord can denote baptized Christians and do not require a biological sibling of an earthly Jesus.
Explain apparent narrative corroborations as consequences of source use, rewriting, literary convention, or selective preservation of authentic incidental material.

sections.title: Pauline Corpus and the Location of Jesus's Career
sections.rationale: Covers the admissible scope of the Pauline corpus and the competing cumulative readings of whether Paul's references locate Jesus's life, death, burial, and resurrection in earthly history or permit a heavenly cosmic setting.

sections.title: The Crucifying Rulers and the Setting of Jesus's Death
sections.rationale: Covers the identity of the rulers in First Corinthians, the surrounding contrast between human and divine wisdom, the relationship to Romans 13, and whether ancient cosmology makes a crucifixion by celestial powers intelligible.

sections.title: Brothers of the Lord and Biological Kinship
sections.rationale: Covers whether Paul's references to James and other brothers of the Lord indicate biological relatives of an earthly Jesus or ordinary baptized Christians, including the limits of using later family traditions to interpret Paul.

sections.title: Luke-Acts as Historically Proximate Pauline Testimony
sections.rationale: Covers authorship, travel-companion claims, first-person narration, Pauline chronology, incidental corroboration, source use, and whether Luke-Acts can connect Paul's circle to a historically situated Jesus tradition.

sections.title: Gospel Correspondences, Independence, and Literary Dependence
sections.rationale: Covers whether interlocking Synoptic and Johannine details support independent historical grounding or are expected from literary adaptation, selective source use, and an author's narrative purposes.

moves.speaker: Richard Carrier

response.rationale: This constructive move offers interlocking incidental Gospel details as source-corroboration evidence, beginning with the feeding narrative and Jesus's choice of Philip.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it presents a recognizable evidentiary method and a concrete example, though the inference to genuine events remains compressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: The general thesis is recoverable, but 'undesigned coincidence,' the relevant Gospel set, and the independence conditions are insufficiently specified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Calling genuine events the best explanation requires comparison with literary dependence, source adaptation, and selective narrative design not yet supplied.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Unexpected interlocking details can support common grounding, but the move leaves the independence and design-exclusion bridges material and unstated.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: A specific feeding example is introduced, yet only its opening puzzle appears and rival literary mechanisms are not compared.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It materially supports subsidiary source corroboration, but Gospel reliability is one step removed from Paul's own conception of Jesus.

representationalCharity.rationale: The constructive span begins the positive example without yet presenting or assessing a developed literary-dependence alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: McLatchie invokes the feeding of the five thousand and asks why John has Jesus address Philip, presenting this as the start of an interlocking-details case.

moves.speaker: Richard Carrier
moves.proposition: John's use and rewriting of earlier Gospels explains apparent interlocking details as designed literary correspondences rather than independent historical corroboration.
moves.attributionBasis: The answer follows McLatchie's invitation to respond and states Carrier's source-dependence explanation in an identifiable opposing turn.

components.text: Whether apparent interlocking Gospel details require independent memory of genuine historical events.
Whether Luke's historical Jesus reliably reflects the understanding of Paul's circle.

response.rationale: Carrier expressly supplies source use and rewriting as an alternative mechanism, defeating the inference from correspondence to independence without addressing Pauline companionship.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply explicitly identifies why the proposed correspondence need not be independent and states the designed-literary consequence.

precisionFindings.rationale: The dependence thesis and rewriting mechanism are clear, though the exact earlier Gospel sources and degree of dependence remain implicit.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The mechanism is plausible, but the span appeals to scholarly prominence rather than demonstrating that the particular correspondence arose through rewriting.

charity.alternative: The dispersed details may be independent memories whose fit was not deliberately constructed by John.
charity.decisiveQualification: Dispersal can support independence, but direct source adaptation can also produce selective explanatory additions and omissions.

logicalCoherence.rationale: If John used earlier Gospels as source material, designed explanatory correspondence follows coherently, with only the dependence premise needing fuller defense.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The span states a recognized source-use hypothesis but does not provide textual markers establishing dependence in the specific feeding example.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It is maximally relevant to the subsidiary literary-correspondence bridge because it directly explains the apparent corroboration through adaptation.

representationalCharity.rationale: Carrier preserves the observed correspondence and gives it an alternative causal explanation rather than denying the relevant details.

moves.evidenceBasis: Carrier argues that John rewrites earlier Gospel source material and may deliberately clarify or reshape details, making the correspondence designed rather than independent.

moves.speaker: Jonathan McLatchie
moves.proposition: The feeding narrative's relevant details are too dispersed and incompletely stated for deliberate reconciliation by the author of John to be plausible.
moves.attributionBasis: The host presses Jonathan to distinguish design from coincidence, and Jonathan answers by tracing where the separate narrative details occur.

components.text: Whether John's use of earlier Gospels plausibly explains the dispersed feeding details as deliberate reconciliation.
Whether incidental accuracy can validate a larger narrative despite contradictions.

response.rationale: McLatchie directly argues that the relevant location and character-origin details are absent from John 6 and scattered elsewhere, challenging deliberate design but not broader source-use possibilities.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it contacts the decisive design-plausibility component but does not exclude an adapter drawing on remembered or external source details.

precisionFindings.rationale: The claim identifies the relevant passages and dispersed details clearly, with the independence inference carrying one bounded implicit qualification.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Dispersal weakens obvious deliberate explanation, but does not establish independence without addressing an adapter's broader source knowledge.

charity.alternative: An adapting author can remember background facts from sources and select appropriate characters without repeating every fact in the scene.
charity.decisiveQualification: Omission and dispersal reduce transparent design but do not make informed character selection implausible.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The scattered placement provides a coherent argument against conspicuous fabrication, but the inference from obscurity to independence remains incomplete.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move names the relevant locations in John 1, John 6, John 12, and Luke 9, while source-access alternatives remain untested.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It sits at the top of subsidiary-tier relevance because it directly attacks the proposed literary-dependence explanation.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply targets deliberate reconciliation fairly but understates the strongest adaptation account, which does not require restating all background details.

moves.evidenceBasis: McLatchie notes that John 6 omits Bethsaida and the origins of Philip and Andrew, while those pieces occur separately in John 1, John 12, and Luke 9.

moves.speaker: Richard Carrier
moves.proposition: An author adapting source material can select characters appropriate to its setting without restating every background detail, so omission of the location does not establish independence.
moves.attributionBasis: Carrier's opposing turn directly explains the author's character selection and omissions through ordinary use of narrative source material.

components.text: Whether omission and dispersal of background details make deliberate Johannine character selection implausible.
Whether the broader pattern of interlocking details is best explained by genuine events.

response.rationale: Carrier expressly explains that an adapter can select fitting characters from source knowledge without restating irrelevant background, defeating the omission-to-independence inference.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply directly diagnoses the inferential failure and gives a concrete alternative process that accounts for both selection and omission.

precisionFindings.rationale: The adaptive mechanism, omitted location detail, and limited conclusion against an independence inference are all clearly recoverable.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move offers an ordinary plausible authorial process rather than claiming certainty that this process generated the passage.

charity.alternative: The character and location fit reflects independent historical memory rather than adaptive selection from literary sources.
charity.decisiveQualification: Independent memory remains possible, but the omission pattern does not discriminate because adaptation predicts selective use as well.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between using background knowledge and narrating every background fact directly defeats the proposed omission inference.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The mechanism fits the cited omissions and character choice, though direct evidence that John possessed and used the relevant source complex remains bounded.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It maximally supports the subsidiary literary-correspondence bridge by answering the strongest dispersed-detail objection.

representationalCharity.rationale: Carrier accepts the dispersed fit and explains why it lacks the discriminatory force claimed, without caricaturing the observed coincidence.

moves.evidenceBasis: Carrier explains that a source-using author can choose Philip or Andrew because they fit the setting while omitting the city and other background facts irrelevant to his narration.
